questionText:
Read the following case study on the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) vs Conventional Puddled Rice, and answer the questions that follow:

Lowland puddled transplanted rice culture is an enormous consumer of fresh water, requiring approximately 3,000 to 5,000 liters of water to produce a single kilogram of milled rice under continuous flooded ponding (5 to 10 cm standing water). Amid escalating groundwater depletion across India, the System of Rice Intensification (SRI)—originally developed in Madagascar by Fr. Henri de Laulanie—has emerged as a resource-conserving paradigm. SRI challenges conventional flood-irrigation dogmas through four synergistic principles: (1) Transplanting very young, single seedlings (8 to 12 days old, at the 2-leaf stage, with the seed sac attached) instead of overaged 25–35 day old bunches, preserving phyllochron tillering potential; (2) Wide square planting geometry (typically 25 x 25 cm or 30 x 30 cm) with single seedlings per hill, providing expansive solar radiation and root volume; (3) Non-flooded water management known as Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), keeping the soil moist but aerobically unsaturated during vegetative growth, and maintaining a shallow 1–2 cm water layer only from panicle initiation to grain dough stage; and (4) Mechanical inter-cultivation using a rotary cono-weeder 2 to 4 times between rows at 10-day intervals. Cono-weeding churns weeds into the soil as in situ green manure while aerating the upper rhizosphere, stimulating profuse, deep root systems and mycorrhizal associations. Field evaluations show SRI reduces irrigation water input by 30% to 40%, slashes seed rate from 40–50 kg/ha down to just 5–7 kg/ha, and increases grain yields by 15% to 30%.

Question: What approximate quantity of certified seed is required to plant one hectare of paddy under the SRI methodology?

options.text: 5 to 7 kg per hectare
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Seed Rate Economy in SRI.

options.text: 500 kg per hectare
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Less than 10 grams
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Seed Rate Economy in SRI (Crop Production):
Planting single seedlings at 25x25 cm requires only 5–7 kg seed/ha, saving over 80% of precious seed volume.
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
